doc.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: July 1953 Balboa sessions with Shorty Rogers
summary: Brown reads out Rendezvous Ballroom jam sessions and Shorty Rogers dates; Holman recalls little beyond a vacation at home.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then I‟m showing some jam sessions in July of ‟53: Shorty Rogers, Conrad Gozzo, Maynard Ferguson, Herb Geller, Jack Montrose, Bill Perkins. They‟ve got you listed as bari. Lorraine Geller on piano, John Simmons, bass, Chuck Flores, drums. It was live at the Rendevous Ballroom, Balboa Beach. Any recollection about that?
That‟s the first entry after your Stan Kenton entries.
Yeah. This is Balboa Beach, July 11, ‟53, live at the Rendevous Ballroom. Tunes: Sometimes I‟m Happy, How High the Moon, Short Snort, Take the “A” Train, C- Jam Blues, The Great Lie, Buzzy.
Oh, I took a vacation. I came home sometime around then. It may have been while I was here. But I don‟t remember it.
Then the next entry is in – actually in July 11, 1953: Jazz Super Stars. Shorty Rogers and his big band.
Yeah. I guess I was in that too.

You‟re credited with tenor and bari on this one. This is also live at the Rendevous Ballroom, Balboa Beach, but again, this is Shorty Rogers, and a pretty extensive repertoire here. Sometimes I‟m Happy, all the way down, Perdido, Nice Work If You Can Get It, Why Shouldn‟t I?No credits for any of the arranging, but it sounds like . . . .

Then the next one is, again, Shorty. So, are you in Shorty‟s band? Because it‟s Shorty Rogers‟s band. Hot Blood is the next entry. It‟s got Shelly on drums, Jimmy Giuffre, Bob Cooper on bari, Jimmy Knepper.
This one is July 14th. So, literally, it‟s almost every day they‟ve got something. But this one was an RCA date, because it was released on RCA records.
It must have been my Shorty Rogers period.
